harness_signal: Nothing in the baseline or the shipped harness names the attachments layer: guren context on the baseline lists no attachments API and the harness templates never mention it, so an agent has to find `guren add` (its help lists it as 'higher-level framework scaffolds') or the Attachable/hasOneAttached exports in @guren/core's types. `guren add attachments` then does most of the plumbing in one step (table, storage config with a private local disk under storage/app, configureAttachments with delivery on, the provider, the delivery route, the prune command) and prints the next steps (db:make, declare collections on the model, keep uploads out of public/). What it leaves: the migration, the Attachable mixin on Post, attach/detach/purgeAttachments in the controller, withAttachments + coverUrl on the resource, and the pages. What no command tells it: hasOneAttached({ image: 'require' }) accepts a GIF (measured; WebP too per the attachments guide) and its only byte cap is the layer-wide maxImageBytes (default 50 MB, a 413 per the guide), so PNG/JPEG-only and 2 MB need a rule of the app's own (the reference puts z.file().max().mime() on the route body contract, which codegen types as `unknown`, so the pages declare their own form type and the controller narrows with instanceof File); destroy must call purgeAttachments() because a polymorphic row cannot cascade; a File left in the validated body reaches forceCreate unless it is destructured out. Traps: the storage blueprint's `public` disk (rooted in public/storage) looks like the natural place for images and guren check reports it as a [fail] for attachments (exit 0, check is informational); attaching after create means bytes that fail the image decode leave a post behind unless the type/size check runs first or the post is deleted when attach() throws (the reference does both); Inertia's useForm sends JSON with cover: null and a boolean removeCover when no file is picked, which a bare z.file().optional() / z.stringbool() refuses. A bare agent may Bun.write the upload into public/uploads (served statically, which the ticket forbids) or a hand-made storage/ directory, add a cover_path column or a hand-rolled attachments table keyed by post_id, serve the bytes with a hand-written Response, and unlink files by hand on replace/delete.
